# Sidekick

**Reverse, fast.**

Search any binary. Understand what it does. Extract what matters.

Sidekick is Binary Ninja's official AI-powered plugin and service for reverse engineering. It is built for real binary analysis work: finding relevant code in stripped targets, repairing decompilation, validating claims against evidence, and keeping your findings organized as the investigation grows.

![Sidekick in Binary Ninja](https://sidekick.binary.ninja/images/hero-screenshot.png)

The plugin is free to install from the Binary Ninja Plugin Manager. Many of Sidekick's service-backed features require a Sidekick plan. Start here:

- Sign in: [https://sidekick.binary.ninja/sign_in](https://sidekick.binary.ninja/sign_in)
- Free trial: [https://sidekick.binary.ninja/free-trial/](https://sidekick.binary.ninja/free-trial/)
- Pricing: [https://sidekick.binary.ninja/pricing/](https://sidekick.binary.ninja/pricing/)
- Getting Started: [https://docs.sidekick.binary.ninja/tutorials/getting-started.html](https://docs.sidekick.binary.ninja/tutorials/getting-started.html)

After installing Sidekick, restart Binary Ninja, open `Plugins > Sidekick > Configure API Key...`, paste an API key from your account, and save. Then open a binary and choose `Plugins > Sidekick > Welcome to Sidekick!` for a guided tour of Search, Simplify, and Surface.

## Find what matters

Point Sidekick at a binary and ask what you need to know. Sidekick's agents can break a broad question into focused searches across the binary, then return a shortlist of relevant functions with evidence you can inspect immediately. On especially large or difficult targets, semantic indexing can help surface the right code even faster.

![Sidekick search results](https://sidekick.binary.ninja/assets/home-search.BwxUqqz9.png)

Learn more: [Search](https://sidekick.binary.ninja/product/search/)

## Make it understandable

Sidekick recovers types, names, class relationships, vtables, and other missing structure from stripped or obfuscated binaries. When the decompiler gets something wrong, such as bad type propagation, collapsed control flow, or broken metadata, Sidekick helps repair the analysis so you can keep moving.

![Recovered decompilation](https://sidekick.binary.ninja/assets/home-simplify-c__-after.BTmbbyxE.png)

Learn more: [Simplify](https://sidekick.binary.ninja/product/simplify/)

## Extract what you need

Findings accumulate in a persistent notebook attached to your analysis. Sidekick helps produce the artifacts your workflow needs, including IOC lists, capability profiles, ATT&CK mappings, and vulnerability assessments, with evidence links preserved for handoff and reporting.

Learn more: [Surface](https://sidekick.binary.ninja/product/surface/)

## Analysis that cross-examines itself

Sidekick does not stop at generating answers. A separate validation flow checks findings against the binary and marks them clearly as draft, verified, or rejected. Claims stay attached to concrete evidence so you can review what matters quickly and keep unsupported conclusions out of your workflow.

Learn more: [Verification](https://sidekick.binary.ninja/product/verification/)

## Works how you work

Sidekick is available as a native Binary Ninja plugin and can also support headless and automated workflows. Hosted plans are available for individuals and teams, and Sidekick can also be deployed self-hosted for private, regulated, or air-gapped environments.

Learn more:

- Features: [https://sidekick.binary.ninja/product/capabilities/](https://sidekick.binary.ninja/product/capabilities/)
- Self-Hosted: [https://sidekick.binary.ninja/product/deployment/](https://sidekick.binary.ninja/product/deployment/)
- FAQ: [https://sidekick.binary.ninja/faq/](https://sidekick.binary.ninja/faq/)

## Requirements

- Binary Ninja 5.3 or newer with an active license
- Linux, macOS, or Windows
- Sidekick service features require a valid Sidekick account and plan
# Release Notes

Sidekick Client Revision: 26.1.516

## Update Instructions

If you are updating from a current installation of the Sidekick plugin, then complete the following instructions:

* Open the Plugin Manager
* Locate the Sidekick plugin
* Click `Update`

After installing or updating, restart Binary Ninja if prompted. To configure service access, open `Plugins > Sidekick > Configure API Key...`, paste an API key from your Sidekick account, and save. With a binary open, choose `Plugins > Sidekick > Welcome to Sidekick!` for the guided onboarding chat.

## Migrating from Sidekick 5x

For further assistance in migrating from Sidekick 5x to the current version, refer to the [migration guide](https://docs.sidekick.binary.ninja/migrating-from-5x.html).

If you need to migrate back to the previous major version, you can download it here: [sidekick-5.0.399.zip](https://plugin.sidekick.binary.ninja/plugins/sidekick-5.0.399.zip).

## Changelog

### Revision 26.1.516

* **Enhancement:** Long-running investigations can now run without an overall turn deadline. The **Maximum Turn Time** setting accepts values up to 99,999 seconds, and setting it to `0` removes the limit entirely, giving you more control over deep research and multi-step workflows. [Read more](https://docs.sidekick.binary.ninja/reference/settings.html#execution)
* **Enhancement:** Python execution limits are now configurable separately for chat and Library scripts. Python code run through chat and Library Python scripts both default to one hour, can be adjusted independently, and can be set to `0` for no timeout. Changes apply immediately to new runs. [Read more](https://docs.sidekick.binary.ninja/guide/library.html#running-python-scripts)
* **Enhancement:** Opening a binary is less disruptive. Sidekick no longer shows a pop-up asking to become your default view; **Prefer Sidekick View** remains disabled by default and can be enabled at any time in Binary Ninja Settings. [Read more](https://docs.sidekick.binary.ninja/guide/sidekick_view.html#setting-it-as-your-default-view)

### Revision 26.1.515

* **Enhancement/Fix:** Faster BNQL lookups and more reliable symbol tracing. [Read more](https://docs.sidekick.binary.ninja/reference/bnql.html#call-graph-functions)
* **Enhancement:** Faster decompilation health checks. Sidekick now inspects each HLIL instruction only once when checking address-taken stack variables, reducing repeated work and keeping analysis more responsive on functions with many stack locals.
* **Enhancement:** Complex investigations can run longer without interruption. The default maximum time for a Sidekick turn has increased from 10 minutes to one hour, giving deep research, repair, and multi-step analysis more time to finish before timing out. You can adjust this limit in Binary Ninja's Sidekick settings. [Read more](https://docs.sidekick.binary.ninja/reference/settings.html#execution)
* **Fix:** The Sidekick pane can now be resized narrower without getting stuck. Long binary names, Session Briefing content, and Work Queue previews no longer impose a hidden minimum width, so Sidekick adapts cleanly when you make room for other Binary Ninja panes. [Read more](https://docs.sidekick.binary.ninja/guide/sidekick_view.html)

### Revision 26.1.514

* **Enhancement:** Choose whether Sidekick should be your default Binary Ninja view. The first time you open a binary after updating, Sidekick explains the center-pane Sidekick view and asks whether you want it to become the preferred default for newly opened binaries. You can change the preference at any time in Settings. [Read more](https://docs.sidekick.binary.ninja/guide/sidekick_view.html#setting-it-as-your-default-view)
* **Fix:** Chat messages now settle to the correct size after Binary Ninja finishes laying out the pane. Messages should no longer appear clipped, compressed, or incorrectly sized when a chat first loads, new content arrives, or the pane is resized. [Read more](https://docs.sidekick.binary.ninja/guide/chat.html)

### Revision 26.1.512

This is the 26.1 feature release. It brings Sidekick into Binary Ninja's center pane as a first-class view, consolidates workspace content into a single Resources sidebar, and adds a durable workspace chat, richer Notebook tracking, versioned repositories, transaction revert, headless chat control, and broad responsiveness and reliability improvements. For an overview of the two headline UI changes, see [What's New in 26.1](https://docs.sidekick.binary.ninja/whats-new-26-1.html).

* **New:** Sidekick is now a center-pane view type. Alongside Linear Disassembly, Graph, and Hex, you can open **Sidekick** as a view that gathers your chat, Session Briefing, and recorded outcomes into one tabbed surface with **Chat**, **Briefing**, **Artifacts**, and **Findings** tabs. With **Prefer Sidekick View** enabled (the default), it is the view a file opens in the first time. [Read more](https://docs.sidekick.binary.ninja/guide/sidekick_view.html)
* **Enhancement:** Workspace content now lives in one place. The separate Indexes, Notebook, Code Maps, and Repositories sidebars have been consolidated into a single **Sidekick Resources** sidebar — one searchable browse list with a shared detail view and pin-to-pane support for notebook entries, indexes, code maps, and workspace repositories. [Read more](https://docs.sidekick.binary.ninja/guide/resources.html)
* **New:** The Chat tab opens on a workspace home. When no chat is active, Sidekick summarizes the current binary and suggests starting points; quick questions are answered in place, while deeper requests are delegated to dedicated work chats that link back and keep running independently. [Read more](https://docs.sidekick.binary.ninja/guide/sidekick_view.html#chat-tab)
* **Enhancement:** The Notebook now tracks blockers, stable task handles, and a live Work Queue. Blockers are first-class entry records with an explicit "needs" ask, tasks carry durable handles that survive restarts, and the Messages drawer shows separate task and blocker counts so you can follow and resume multi-step work. [Read more](https://docs.sidekick.binary.ninja/guide/notebook.html#working-with-tasks)
* **Enhancement:** The Session Briefing keeps itself current. Meaningful Notebook changes now trigger a bounded, debounced re-synthesis of the rolling workspace summary, so the briefing reflects recent findings without your having to request a refresh. [Read more](https://docs.sidekick.binary.ninja/guide/notebook.html#session-briefing)
* **New:** Workspace repositories are versioned. Sidekick can record Markdown reports and other files as committed revisions that stay pinned and resolvable over time, browsable from Resources and the Library with history, a rendered README, and read-only past revisions. [Read more](https://docs.sidekick.binary.ninja/guide/library.html#workspace-repositories)
* **New:** Review and undo committed analysis changes. A committed transaction now shows a grouped before/after patch you can read and copy, and a guarded **Revert** applies an inverse transaction that restores prior values without clobbering edits you made afterward. [Read more](https://docs.sidekick.binary.ninja/guide/transaction_log.html#undoing-changes)
* **New:** Manage Sidekick chats headlessly. Through the Sidekick API and the bundled MCP server you can now create, call, resume, list, inspect, rename, and remove chats — driving the full agent from automation and external tools. [Read more](https://docs.sidekick.binary.ninja/guide/sidekick_api.html#call-the-sidekick-service-agent)
* **New:** Sidekick can run terminal commands on your machine. With the `run_terminal_command` tool and your permission, the agent can execute command-line programs — `curl`, `docker`, build and analysis tools, and more — dramatically extending what it can do beyond Binary Ninja itself. Terminal execution is permission-gated: every command requires your approval before it runs. [Read more](https://docs.sidekick.binary.ninja/guide/chat.html#tool-approval-and-permissions)
* **Enhancement/Fix:** External MCP tools are more reliable. Sidekick now discovers every tool a server offers, even large servers that paginate their tool list, so tools past the first page are no longer silently missing. Tool **aliases** work correctly, letting you rename tools to avoid collisions when two servers expose the same name. Server sessions are reused while healthy and shut down cleanly on exit, and the configured `timeout` now applies to initialization, discovery, and each tool call. [Read more](https://docs.sidekick.binary.ninja/guide/mcp_tools.html)
* **Enhancement:** Open project members from chat. In a Binary Ninja project, Sidekick can list project files and open a closed member into the shared workspace by ID or unique name, disambiguating same-named files instead of guessing. [Read more](https://docs.sidekick.binary.ninja/guide/multiple_binaries.html#opening-and-closing-individual-binaries)
* **Enhancement:** Chats stay responsive as workspaces grow, and stopping is reliable. Large histories load and scroll without stutter, and pressing **stop** (or **Escape**) now cleanly cancels the active turn and the entire tree of child threads and scripts it spawned. [Read more](https://docs.sidekick.binary.ninja/guide/chat.html#the-message-composer)
* **Enhancement:** Compact long conversations on demand. Submitting `/compact` summarizes a settled chat and continues it on a successor thread, keeping the conversation readable and within context while preserving earlier facts. [Read more](https://docs.sidekick.binary.ninja/guide/chat.html#the-message-composer)
* **Enhancement:** Evidence is easier to follow. Assistant replies group their citations into evidence chips that open an anchored card of references, and reference links navigate to the exact code, notebook outcome, transaction, index, code map, or repository file — single-click to sync navigation and double-click to open the location. [Read more](https://docs.sidekick.binary.ninja/guide/chat.html#tool-groups)
* **Enhancement:** More precise BNQL over program structure. Segment and section containment traversal now terminates correctly and returns the right contained objects, data-variable results carry accurate navigation tokens, and newly created BNQL indexes name themselves until you rename them. [Read more](https://docs.sidekick.binary.ninja/reference/bnql.html#structural-axes)
* **Enhancement:** Automation scripts are trustworthy. Library and trigger scripts report truthful completed/failed/cancelled/timed-out states, retain complete paged output, accept arguments and timeouts, and interrupt cleanly without poisoning later runs. [Read more](https://docs.sidekick.binary.ninja/guide/library.html#running-python-scripts)
* **Enhancement:** Configurable request timeouts and recoverable errors. You can set a per-endpoint request timeout, and a timed-out or failed turn now surfaces a readable error card with working Retry and Dismiss actions instead of a stalled chat. [Read more](https://docs.sidekick.binary.ninja/guide/chat.html#clearing-errors)
* **Enhancement:** Safer workspace handling. Closing a never-saved workspace that contains chats or resources now warns before discarding your work, and exporting or importing large workspaces shows determinate progress while keeping the UI responsive. [Read more](https://docs.sidekick.binary.ninja/guide/sharing_data.html)

### Revision 26.0.499

* **Fix:** The Chats sidebar now stays responsive as chat history grows. Workspaces with lots of chats and long conversations should no longer stutter or hang the Binary Ninja UI. [Read more](https://docs.sidekick.binary.ninja/guide/chat.html)

### Revision 26.0.498

* **Fix:** Stopping a chat now reliably halts everything it set in motion. Pressing the **stop button** (or simply pressing `Escape` while a chat is busy) cancels not just the active turn but the entire tree of subagents and child threads it spawned, so nothing keeps running in the background after you ask it to stop. [Read more](https://docs.sidekick.binary.ninja/guide/chat.html#the-message-composer)
* **Fix:** Stopping a running script now also stops the chats it launched. When you stop a Library script — from the Library sidebar or one started from a chat — Sidekick now propagates the cancellation into any Sidekick chat threads that script kicked off, so a single stop fully unwinds the work instead of leaving an agent conversation running on its own. [Read more](https://docs.sidekick.binary.ninja/guide/library.html#running-python-scripts)

### Revision 26.0.497

* **Enhancement/Fix:** Cleaner string content in semantic search. Sidekick now filters out extraneous strings that Binary Ninja's scanner picks up from instruction bytes and other noise, and it renders the strings it does index with better surrounding context. The result is more
relevant concept() search results and a more compact, less cluttered index. You can tune the admission thresholds in Binary Ninja's Settings panel under the Sidekick group. [Read more](https://docs.sidekick.binary.ninja/guide/semantic_indexing.html#adjusting-string-admission-filters)
* **Enhancement:** Query structure members and data variable sizes in BNQL. Sidekick can now traverse the members of structures and unions
and read the size of data variables directly in BNQL. This gives both the agent and your own queries a more precise view of types and data layout, improving type recovery and data-flow analysis. [Read more](https://docs.sidekick.binary.ninja/reference/bnql.html#type-system-axes)
* **Enhancement/Fix:** Suggest Types is more reliable on large functions. When recovering types, Sidekick now reads the target function with bounded, focused context instead of pulling the entire function body up front, then makes targeted follow-up reads only where it
needs more detail. This avoids stalls and wasted effort on very large functions while still producing accurate type suggestions. [Read more](https://docs.sidekick.binary.ninja/guide/suggestions.html#suggest-types)
* **Enhancement:** The Notebook now keeps a record of completed work. As Sidekick works through a multi-step task, it marks each task complete when it finishes rather than deleting it, so the Notebook retains a visible history of what was done across turns and
sessions. This makes it easier to follow the agent's progress and to pick an investigation back up later. [Read more](https://docs.sidekick.binary.ninja/guide/notebook.html#working-with-tasks)
* **Fix:** In some situations, Sidekick caused Binary Ninja to hang while a binary loads on restart. This has been fixed. Reopening a binary that already has Sidekick data — chats, indexes, and metadata — stays responsive while that data is restored, even for workspaces with a large amount of stored history.

### Revision 26.0.494

* **Enhancement:** Library agent slash commands now stay connected to the current chat. When running an agent Library item by entering `/<agent-name> ...` from the Chat, Sidekick delegates the work to a child thread and posts the final result back into the original conversation. This allows Sidekick to see your subagent's output and respond appropriately, making agent slash commands behave more like Library scripts and skills. [Read more](https://docs.sidekick.binary.ninja/guide/chat.html#composer-library-slash-commands)
* **Enhancement:** The main Sidekick agent can now search the Library to see what scripts, skills, and agents are available and how to use them. This makes it easier to choose the right Library item before launching it. [Read more](https://docs.sidekick.binary.ninja/guide/library.html#the-library-sidebar)
* **Enhancement/Fix:** Library Python scripts now launch more reliably from chat and automation when no specific revision or inputs are needed. If no revision is selected, Sidekick runs the current working copy, and scripts that do not take arguments no longer fail just because an empty argument payload was provided. [Read more](https://docs.sidekick.binary.ninja/guide/library.html#running-python-scripts)
* **Enhancement:** When using the API to write scripts for headless or UI operation, you can now use the built-in Sidekick chat agent, not just custom local agents. This allows you to leverage the tools, skills, and intelligence of the main Sidekick agent in your automation. [Read more](https://docs.sidekick.binary.ninja/guide/sidekick_api.html#call-the-sidekick-service-agent)

### Revision 26.0.487

This release is a major redesign of Sidekick. It introduces agentic reverse engineering workflows, a revamped UI, expanded API and project support, and new capabilities like semantic search, MCP integration, and transaction logging.

* **Enhancement:** Introduced specialist modes for Research, Transform, Repair Analysis, Modeling, Debugger, and Automation workflows.
* **New:** Added a validation agent that cross-checks findings against IL, assembly, and memory traces, and repairs analysis issues when needed.
* **New:** Added a persistent Behavioral Model to carry forward descriptions of binary behavior across sessions outside the BNDB.
* **Enhancement:** Expanded the Notebook to track goals, tasks, findings, artifacts, blockers, and outcomes with explicit status.
* **New:** Added reusable Skills playbooks that load based on context for common reverse engineering tasks.
* **Enhancement:** Revamped the UI with an inspectable chat tree so subagent work is fully visible.
* **New:** Added Code Maps for auto-built call graphs and manual JSON diagrams with live index entries inside function nodes.
* **Enhancement:** Improved indexes with BNQL, Script, and Manual modes, sortable metadata fields, and support across all binaries in a project.
* **New:** Added a Suggest menu for repairs, types, names, and comments.
* **New:** Expanded the Sidekick API with completion pools, model templates, and headless `sidekick()` access for full-workspace automation from Python.
* **Enhancement:** Added Binary Ninja Project support with a shared workspace, cross-binary BNQL, and project-scoped AI across multiple binaries.
* **New:** Added semantic search powered by a local vector database, with the `concept()` operator available in BNQL, chat, and scripts.
* **New:** Added MCP support so Sidekick can use external tools through Model Context Protocol servers.
* **New:** Added debugger specialist mode for breakpoint-driven runtime observation with resumable threads.
* **New:** Added hierarchical tool permissions scoped per chat, per workspace, or globally.
* **New:** Added a transaction log so every database change is tracked and can be undone step by step.

# Unpac.Me Plugin (v1.2)

Author: **Vector 35 Inc**

_Simple plugin to interface Binary Ninja with the UnpacMe automatic unpacking service_

## Description:

This plugin lets you easily submit binaries and download unpacked results from [unpac.me](https://unpac.me/).

You will first need to sign up for a free account before you can use it. The first time you try to upload or download you will be prompted for your API Key which is available from your [account page](https://www.unpac.me/account).

Current features:

- Upload a file to be unpacked. Available from the `Plugins/UnpacMe` menu and command-palette, works on the currently open file.
- Download a previously extracted file. Available from the `Plugins/UnpacMe` menu and command-palette.

![](https://github.com/Vector35/unpacme/blob/master/media/download.png?raw=true)
![](https://github.com/Vector35/unpacme/blob/master/media/menu.png?raw=true)

## Installation Instructions

Use the plugin manager or clone this to your [user plugin folder](https://docs.binary.ninja/getting-started.html#user-folder).

## Minimum Version

This plugin requires the following minimum version of Binary Ninja:

* 3469

## Troubleshooting

If you receive python errors, you may need to upgrade your version of python to support requests with HTTPS support.

## License

This plugin is released under a MIT license.

## Metadata Version

2

### Changelog
**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/Vector35/unpacme/compare/1.1...1.2

# Snippet UI Plugin
Author: **Vector 35 Inc**

_Powerful code-editing plugin for writing and managing python code-snippets with syntax highlighting, hotkey binding and other features_

## Description:

The snippet editor started as a simple example UI plugin to demonstrate new features available to UI plugins. It has turned into a functionally useful plugin in its own right. The snippet editor allows you to write small bits of code that might not be big enough to warrant the effort of a full plugin but are long enough that you don't want to retype them every time in the python-console!

As an added bonus, all snippets are added to the snippets menu and hot-keys can be associated with them as they make use of the action system. All action-system items are also available through the command-palette (CTL/CMD-p).

![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Vector35/snippets/refs/heads/master/media/snippets.gif)

## Installation Instructions

### Darwin

no special instructions, package manager is recommended

### Linux

no special instructions, package manager is recommended

### Windows

no special instructions, package manager is recommended

## Minimum Version

This plugin requires the following minimum version of Binary Ninja:

* 1528

## Required Dependencies

The following dependencies are required for this plugin:

 * pip - pygments>=2.7.0,<2.9.0

This Binary Ninja UI plugin allows you to browse a hex dump within Binary Ninja with a tree view informed by [Kaitai Struct](https://kaitai.io/).

![](https://github.com/Vector35/kaitai/blob/master/media/kaitai.gif?raw=true)

This wires up Kaitai Struct as a parsing library to produce templated dissection of binary files. Of course, this concept itself isn’t new. Plenty of great tools like 010, Hexinator and Synalyze It! have this feature (last two by the same company for different platforms). Thanks to the Kaitai Project not only for the project in general, but also for working with us to resolve some small issues while we were developing the plugin.

## License

This plugin is released under a MIT license.



### Changelog
- Removes the unused import for `audioop`.  It was officially deprecated in Python 3.11 and removed in Python 3.13 as part of [PEP 594](https://peps.python.org/pep-0594/#audioop).  This was causing plugin load errors on more recent Python interpreters. (#11)

# Blob Extractor
Author: **Vector 35 Inc.**

_Binary Ninja plugin for extracting files from container formats_

![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Vector35/blob_extractor/master/preview.png)


## Description

Blob Extractor is a Binary Ninja plugin that leverages the [Unblob API](https://github.com/onekey-sec/unblob) to
identify and extract compressed archives, file-systems, and other blobs embedded in container binaries such as flash
dumps or firmware images.


## Installation Instructions

The following dependencies are required by this plugin:

* [unblob](https://github.com/onekey-sec/unblob) - Python package for extracting files from container formats
* libmagic - Native libmagic file type identification library
* [python-magic](https://github.com/ahupp/python-magic) - Python bindings for libmagic

If the plugin is installed from the Binary Ninja plugin manager, the Python dependencies should install
automatically. However, the `libmagic` native library must be installed manually. The instructions below provide
guidance on how to install the plugin and its dependencies manually. Step 1 is required for all installation methods.  



### Darwin

1. Install the `libmagic` native library

```
brew install libmagic
```

2. Clone the repository into the Binary Ninja `plugins` directory (or install from the Binary Ninja plugin manager)

```
git clone git@github.com:Vector35/blob_extractor.git "/Users/$USER/Library/Application Support/Binary Ninja/plugins/blob_extractor"
```

3. Install the dependency Python packages for the Python version in use by Binary Ninja. These packages should be
installed from the `requirements.txt` file, included in the plugin repository.

```
cd "/Users/$USER/Library/Application Support/Binary Ninja/plugins/blob_extractor"
pip3 install -r requirements.txt
``` 


### Linux

1. Install the `libmagic` native library

```
sudo apt-get install libmagic1
```

2. Clone the repository into the Binary Ninja `plugins` directory (or install from the Binary Ninja plugin manager)

```
git clone git@github.com:Vector35/blob_extractor.git ~/.binaryninja/plugins/blob_extractor
```

3. Install the dependency Python packages for the Python version in use by Binary Ninja. These packages should be
installed from the `requirements.txt` file, included in the plugin repository.

```
cd ~/.binaryninja/plugins/blob_extractor
pip3 install -r requirements.txt
```  



### Windows

Windows is not supported by this plugin. Blob Extractor depends on `libmagic`, Unblob, and Unblob's extractor utilities.
These dependencies do not run on Windows. 


## Extractor Utilities

Unblob uses external utilities for file extraction. After installing Unblob (via the installation instructions above)
run the following command to identify missing external extractor utilities:

```
> unblob --show-external-dependencies
The following executables found installed, which are needed by unblob:
    7z                          ✓
    debugfs                     ✗
    jefferson                   ✓
    lz4                         ✓
    lziprecover                 ✓
    lzop                        ✓
    sasquatch                   ✗
    sasquatch-v4be              ✗
    simg2img                    ✓
    ubireader_extract_files     ✓
```

_Note: unblob is installed at `~/.local/bin/unblob` on Linux._

Missing extractor utilities must be installed manually. Linux users can install the majority of the external
dependencies using `apt`. MacOS users can use `brew`. Some of the external dependencies, such as `sasquatch`, must be
built from source. Blob Extractor will still run without external extractor utilities. However, it will be unable to
extract certain blob formats. See the [Install Extractors](https://unblob.org/installation/#install-extractors) section
from the Unblob documentation for more information. 


## Troubleshooting

**The plugin icon is not appearing in the Binary Ninja sidebar**

This is most likely because the plugin dependencies have not been installed properly and the plugin failed to load. It
is recommended to open the Binary Ninja log and see if there is a Python traceback originating from Blob Extractor. The
traceback should indicate what the issue is. If you are unable to run `unblob` from the command-line, it likely won't
run from the plugin either. Be sure to follow the installation steps above and verify that `unblob` and its dependencies
are installed correctly by running `unblob --show-external-dependencies` from your terminal.

**The plugin is not extracting any files, or extracted files are empty**

This is most likely because the required external dependencies for Unblob have not been installed. For example, if
you're extracting a flash dump that contains a squash file system, you must have sasquatch installed on your system. For
JFFS2 you need jefferson, and so on. See the `Extractor Utilities` section above. Also reference the
[Install Extractors](https://unblob.org/installation/#install-extractors) section from the Unblob documentation.


## License

This plugin is released under an [MIT license](./LICENSE).

# Tantō
Author: **Vector 35, Inc.**

## Description:
Tantō is a plugin for [Binary Ninja](https://binary.ninja/) that slices programs so you can understand them faster.

![slices](https://github.com/Vector35/tanto/blob/master/tanto_preview.png?raw=true)

For a more detailed explanation of what Tantō does, please check out [this blog post](https://binary.ninja/2022/06/20/introducing-tanto.html).

## Minimum Version

This plugin requires the following minimum version of Binary Ninja:

* 4.0.5336

## License

This plugin has been released under the [MIT license](./LICENSE.txt).
